data.title: Trump officials met privately with investors on Norfolk/Union Pacific deal - Bloomberg
data.description:
Trump officials met privately with a group of hedge fund investors who are betting on the outcome of Union Pacific's (UNP) $72 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern (NSC).

The meeting included investors from several major hedge funds and multiple officials from Trump's administration, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. The funds that attended the meeting specialize in merger arbitrage.

Administration officials didn't share non-public information at the meeting, according to the report.

A White House official said in a statement to Bloomberg that a junior staffer, who no longer works at the White House, attended a lunch off the White House complex and that his attendance wasn’t authorized.

Union Pacific (UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NSC) filed a response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City's (CP) request that the Surface Transportation Board terminate review of the merger application for a transcontinental railroad.

The Dept. of Justice is expected to give its opinion on the deal by Dec. 3. The DOJ is likely to remain neutral on the rail combination, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report at the time.

The STB is expected to issue its final decision within 90 days of the record closing, targeting final approval and transaction completion by late summer 2027.

data.title: Wall Street sinks as the tech space remains under heavy pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were lower on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.7%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -2.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -3.6%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, five of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area. 

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities. 

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 12 basis points to 4.65%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted down 10 basis points to 4.94%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved down 7 basis points to 5.33%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) advanced +5.2%, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) dropped -14.4%.

data.title: Nestlé looks to tech giants to automate production -- WSJ
data.description:
Nestlé (NSRGY) is looking to automate its production lines and is working with tech giants to develop AI-powered robots that will be able to run manufacturing and make decisions with little to no human intervention.

“At a certain point in time you can put agentic AI on top of it, and then it’s orchestrating the entire flow. The fully autonomous line is one of the future. We will still need our experts, because we need expert judgment in most cases,” said Nestlé's technology chief Stefan Palzer to The Wall Street Journal.

Nestlé (NSRGY) is working with Microsoft (MSFT) and Boston Dynamics to develop AI and engineering solutions and exploring potential partnerships with Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) and Apple (AAPL).

With the aim to “drive business growth,” Palzer said that these partnerships will enable Nestle’s production lines to fully understand and adapt to variable inputs and produce consistent output.

An increased dependence on automation and artificial intelligence in the food industry comes with unique challenges but will help facilitate operational efficiencies and enable manufacturing to better adapt to changing consumer habits.

“Technology can help with reformulation and product development, but execution will matter more than the tools,” an analyst with Swiss bank Vontobel said to the WSJ.

data.title: S&P 500 enters correction territory and these 20 names are fueling the leg lower
data.description:

On Friday afternoon, the benchmark index continued to retreat, falling 2% in the session and hovering near 7,033. The latest levels mark the lowest stance since April 16, establishing a seven-month trading low.

The sustained pullback reflects growing caution among investors as the broad market extends its recent losses. data.title: Seven funds trim positions in Taiwan Semiconductor in Q3
data.description:
Several hedge funds and institutional holders decreased their holdings in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) this quarter, while some increased, and only one initiated a new position in the stock.

Larry Robbins and Mark Horowitz owned Glenview Capital, built a new position in the company with 71,104 shares worth $32.44M.

Among those who added to their existing holdings in the firm were Soros Fund, Viking Global, and Lone Pine. The George Soros-owned fund inched up its holdings by 5% Q/Q to 548,915 shares. Viking Global boosted its holdings to 3.90M shares, translating to a 23% sequential rise. Lone Pine jacked up its stake to 1.72M shares from 101,242 shares.

Softbank and Altimeter Capital maintained their positions in TSMC at 565,000 and 1.43M shares, respectively.

Notably, seven hedge funds or holders trimmed their positions in the Taiwanese semiconductor giant in the third quarter. The biggest reduction came from Stanley Druckenmiller’s Duquesne Family Office, which slashed its holdings by 94% to 32,700 shares.

Robert Soros's Soros Capital decreased its holdings to 27,664 shares. Douglas Silverman’s Senator Investment Group reduced its holdings to 185,658 shares.

Lansdowne Partners cut TSMC’s stake to 1.41M shares. However, it continued to occupy the top spot in its portfolio. Tiger Global reduced its position to 3.13M shares. Appaloosa brought its holdings down to 1.58M shares, and Third Point decreased its holdings to 400,000 shares.

data.title: Arizona AG asks local zoning board to delay vote on SpaceX's $50B data center: report
data.description:
Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes has requested a local zoning commission in the state to tap the brakes on an upcoming vote for SpaceX's (SPCX) proposed $50B data center, according to Bloomberg.

The Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission is scheduled to vote on a special use permit for the facility on December 9.

"This delay is necessary to ensure that the County does not begin authorizing a project with potentially far-reaching impacts on the region's energy reliability, water availability, and resident health and safety until it has been thoroughly vetted by the relevant state and federal regulatory authorities," Mayes said in a letter to commissioners, according to the report.

Mayes plans to hold a community meeting in the county on December 3.

"Working with local electric cooperatives, the project aims to strengthen regional energy infrastructure, leverage existing renewable resources, and potentially reduce electricity bills for cooperative members by up to 20% while using dry cooling with no planned industrial groundwater consumption," SpaceX said of the project.

SpaceX is also in the process of adding $24B in AI infrastructure at its facility in Brownsville, Texas. Earlier this week, Cameron County Commissioners voted against moving forward on a hearing to consider a tax abatement on the new data center.

"Property owners could now face greater year-to-year fluctuations in tax rates as the equipment depreciates," SpaceX said of the decision in a post on X. "The agreement was intended to provide more predictable County revenue while supporting continued investment in the region. We look forward to continued discussions with local jurisdictions on how to maximize the economic benefits of these investments while protecting sustainable, long-term tax revenues."

SpaceX shares declined nearly 7% by noon trading on Friday.

data.title: Belite Bio drops on FDA review extension for tinlarebant NDA
data.description:
• Belite Bio (BLTE) is down ~13% Friday after the US FDA said it would delay by three months the PDUFA date for the company's NDA for tinlarebant for Stargardt disease type 1.
  • The new action date is May 12, 2027.
  • The company noted that the agency said that if no major issues are found during the ongoing review, it will communicate proposed labeling requests and any anticipated postmarketing requirement requests by April 12.
  • Tinlarebant is an oral treatment designed to reduce the accumulation of vitamin A-based toxins, known as bisretinoids, that cause retinal disease in Stargardt disease type 1.

data.title: Hewlett Packard Q4 preview: What to expect
data.description:
Analysts expect Hewlett Packard (HPE) to benefit from healthy enterprise infrastructure spending, strong networking demand, and improving storage trends when it reports fourth-quarter earnings on November 23rd, after the closing bell.

The consensus EPS estimate is $1.29, while the consensus revenue estimate is $14.43B—falling within management’s raised guidance range of $1.20 and $1.30 and $13.9 billion and $14.8 billion, respectively.

Heading into the earnings, analysts at Citi saw a constructive setup for enterprise hardware providers like HPE and Dell (DELL) on the back of pent-up enterprise infrastructure demand, healthy AI backlogs, and operational/supply-chain efficiencies to navigate volatility.

Ahead of the earnings, analysts are bullish about the firm, with EPS estimates seeing 17 upward revisions and revenue estimates seeing 15 upward moves over the last 3 months, with neither witnessing any downward adjustments.

A large part of this optimism is being driven by the networking segment, which experts believe will drive around 40% of segment profit by fiscal 2027.

“It (HPE) has more than doubled its networking purchase commitments, while the company's total binding purchase obligations, mostly related to inventory, have reached roughly nine times their level at the end of FY25,” Seeking Alpha analyst Vishal Jadaun said.

The company upped the growth outlook of the networking business to the high teens to low 20s in FY27 and margins to the mid-to-high 20s, Jadaun added.

Moreover, Citi analysts also noted that the quarter could be positive for shareholders, with management targeting a resumption of share buybacks in F4Q.

“With management targeting a return to buybacks in F4Q, supported by strong FCF generation, we see an attractive shareholder return profile,” Asiya Merchant said.

Over the last 2 years, HPE has beaten EPS estimates 88% of the time and has beaten revenue estimates 75% of the time.

data.title: Flight to safety drives Treasury yields lower as tech tumbles
data.description:
U.S. Treasury yields declined across the curve on Friday afternoon as equity markets came under pressure, prompting investors to shift into government bonds for relative safety.

The move reflected a classic flight-to-quality response. With stocks selling off, demand for Treasuries increased, driving yields lower.

The front end of the curve led the decline: the U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y)  fell 11 basis points to 4.65%, the largest drop among the major maturities. The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) dropped 10 basis points to 4.94%, while the longer-end U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) eased 7 basis points to 5.33%.

The coordinated retreat underscored heightened caution among market participants. Bond purchases accelerated as equity losses mounted, tightening yields, especially in shorter-dated paper that is more sensitive to near-term shifts in risk appetite and rate expectations.

The session illustrated the ongoing interplay between equities and fixed income. When stock prices weaken, Treasuries frequently absorb the resulting capital flows, producing the inverse relationship observed Friday.
